module: Second step of vehicle loading, on the vehicle VM side: takes the jbeam data already assembled by the game (stage 1, in the game VM) and "pushes" it into the C++ physics by calling obj:setNode, obj:setBeam, obj:setWheel, obj:addRail, obj:addSlidenode, obj:setTorsionbar, obj:setTriangle, obj:setReferenceNodes then obj:finishLoading. main.lua loads it as the global `v` (v = require('jbeam/stage2')): after loadVehicleStage2, `v.data` contains the vehicle data (nodes, beams, wheels, hydros, powertrain, refNodes, input, information…), and `v.config` the configuration (parts, paints, additionalVehicleData…). It is therefore the source of all jbeam reads by the other modules.
usage:
-- in a vehicle module (after spawn):
for _, node in pairs(v.data.nodes) do print(node.name, node.cid, node.pos.x) end
local wheelLock = v.data.input and v.data.input.steeringWheelLock
local partConfig = v.config.parts
notes: Order of sending to the physics (pushToPhysics): obj:requestReset(RESET_PHYSICS), then nodes, beams, wheels, rails, slidenodes, torsionhydros, torsionbars, collision triangles, reference nodes, finally obj:finishLoading(). Each element receives a `cid` field (identifier on the C++ side) assigned by the setXxx.
Beam types (values defined in C, do not modify): normal 0, anisotropic 1, bounded 2, pressured 3, lbeam 4, broken 5, support 7. Node types: normal 0, fixed 1, noncollidable 2.

Useful defaults: beamStrength = vehicle.options.beamStrength or math.huge (unbreakable); a beamStrength as a string is accepted if it represents a number. A degenerate triangle is reported by an error log. If the reference nodes (refNodes[0]) are missing, dummy nodes (ref 0, back 1, left 2, up 0) are installed with an error log.

loadVehicleStage2 sets vdata.format = 'parsed', publishes M.data, M.config and, for compatibility, M.vehicleDirectory = M.data.vehicleDirectory, and measures the loading time (log 'Vehicle loading took: … ms').
This module only runs once per spawn (called by main.lua:init). Later modifications of v.data are not sent back to the C++ physics: they only affect the Lua modules.

data.desc: Vehicle data (vdata stage 1): nodes, beams, wheels, rails, slidenodes, torsionbars, torsionHydros, hydros, triangles, refNodes, powertrain, input, information, flexbodies, activeParts, activePartsData, etc. Set by loadVehicleStage2 (main.lua creates an empty table if absent).

config.desc: Vehicle configuration (parts, paints, additionalVehicleData…). Set by loadVehicleStage2.

vehicleDirectory.desc: Vehicle directory (copy of data.vehicleDirectory, for backward compatibility).

loadVehicleStage2.desc: Sends the jbeam data to the physics (nodes, beams, wheels, rails, slidenodes, torsions, triangles, reference nodes) then publishes v.data and v.config. Called once by main.lua:init with the decoded spawn data.

vdataStage1.desc: Spawn table {vdata = assembled jbeam data, config = vehicle configuration}.

returns.desc: vdata (the vehicle data) on success; nil if vdata is not a table.
